title: Review AirNow API terms of use for compliance
description:
Research complete 2026-07-27; decision made 2026-07-28. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review -- research findings' for the full writeup.

OPERATIVE AGREEMENT: no separate API ToS; the EPA AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines PDF (docs.airnowapi.org/docs/DataUseGuidelines.pdf, updated Aug 2025) is what registration agrees to. Confirmed by fetching both the registration page and the PDF.

FINDINGS: nothing prohibits redistribution. The API FAQ explicitly endorses the caching pattern this project uses ('cache daily or hourly... populate your own database'), with one caveat (no bulk zip-code enumeration) that opportunistic per-request caching doesn't trigger.

DECISION: caching and redistributing AirNow data via a proxy server is permitted. Service mode proceeds alongside Direct mode.

OBLIGATIONS identified during review -- unaffected by this decision, tracked separately, gating App Store submission rather than the start of implementation:
  1. Two-tier attribution (specific agency first, then AirNow/EPA): 10h.15, e70.10, mtm.14
  2. In-product preliminary-data disclaimer: dc2.4
  3. Official EPA AQI colors, binding via incorporation into the Guidelines: 10h.2
  4. Never derive AQI client-side: 10h.17
  5. Notify AirNow the product exists: 8ef.13
  6. Keep AirNow contact info current: 8ef.14
Full set: bd list --label compliance
close_reason: Reviewed and approved by the project owner 2026-07-28: caching and redistributing AirNow data via a proxy server is permitted, so Service mode proceeds. Unblocks all implementation. Compliance obligations remain tracked under the 'compliance' label and gate App Store submission, not implementation start.

title: Select and document the AirNow endpoint(s) to call
description:
The API Fact Sheet enumerates several web services with meaningful differences, and the design has been loosely referencing 'currentobservation/latLong' without confirming it's the right one:

  - Current Observations by Reporting Area -- 'Real-time air quality observations (NowCast AQI) for each pollutant measured by reporting areas -- cities or other reporting areas DEFINED BY AIR QUALITY AGENCIES.' Appears to match our needs on all three axes: NowCast, per-pollutant breakdown (widget scope), and reporting-area scoping.
  - Observations by Monitoring Site -- site-level rather than aggregated.
  - Forecasts / Historical Observations by Reporting Area / Contour Maps -- not v1.

Confirm which endpoint actually returns: (a) NowCast AQI, (b) the full per-pollutant breakdown the widget scope requires, (c) the owning agency name for attribution, and (d) a category descriptor, or whether we derive the category from the value against the TAD table (allowed -- that's classification of a received AQI, not computing an AQI; distinct from bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

The 'reporting areas defined by air quality agencies' phrasing is likely where attribution comes from -- airnow.gov showed 'San Francisco Reporting Area' and 'Data courtesy of Bay Area Air District' together. Feeds directly into bluegull-aqi-10h.15. Record the answer in doc/DESIGN.md.

title: Never derive AQI client-side; display values as received
description:
HARD CONSTRAINT from two independent sources. The AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require data be 'disseminated as received' without alteration. The TAD independently states it is 'not valid to use shorter-term (e.g. hourly) data to calculate an AQI value.'

So: display AirNow's AQI values exactly as returned. NEVER convert a pollutant concentration into an AQI, never re-derive, never interpolate, never round differently than received. The TAD's breakpoint table (Table 5) and interpolation formula (Equation 1) are in the design doc as documentation of what NOT to implement -- they are the agency-side calculation, not ours.

If the API returns a raw concentration for some pollutant WITHOUT an accompanying AQI value, display the concentration labeled as a concentration (with units) -- do not compute an index from it.

Include a test asserting no AQI-derivation logic exists in the codebase (e.g. no breakpoint table, no interpolation against one), so this can't be reintroduced later by someone trying to 'fill in' a missing value. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.

title: Round coordinates client-side before transmission
description:
Privacy by design, and free. The service otherwise receives precise coordinates and logs requests, accumulating 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' in CloudWatch for the whole retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database, and a poor fit for an app whose purpose is local environmental data.

AirNow resolves to the nearest monitoring station regardless, so ~1km precision loses no accuracy AND improves cache hit rates. Round before the request leaves the Mac so the server never receives a precise location at all. Applies to both Direct and Service mode.

title: Set up AWS Budget alarms before first deploy
description: Five minutes of setup; the difference between noticing a cost attack in an hour and noticing it on the monthly invoice. Must exist BEFORE the first deploy, not after. Set a low absolute threshold plus an anomaly-detection alert, since normal spend for this service should be near zero.

title: Add cost circuit breakers: reserved concurrency + API Gateway throttling
description:
Denial of wallet is the primary threat on this architecture. Lambda, API Gateway, and on-demand DynamoDB all scale elastically, so they all BILL elastically -- a sustained flood costs money at a rate nothing in the base design bounds. Per-IP WAF rate limiting does little against a botnet, and WAF bills per request itself, amplifying cost under attack rather than capping it.

  - Lambda reserved concurrency: a hard ceiling on concurrent executions and therefore on cost per unit time. This is the PRIMARY circuit breaker, not just a noisy-neighbor courtesy -- note the existing scale-config task frames it that way and should be read together with this one.
  - API Gateway stage throttling: hard request-rate cap, independent of WAF.
  - DynamoDB on-demand has no ceiling by design; the Lambda cap is what indirectly bounds it.

title: Validate coordinates and reject out-of-coverage requests
description:
Closes the cache-cardinality attack, which the stampede mitigation does NOT cover: stale-while-revalidate + single-flight collapses concurrent requests for the SAME key, so an attacker requesting a million DISTINCT coordinates produces a million cache misses, each triggering an upstream AirNow call -- burning the AirNow quota (likely getting the key banned), filling DynamoDB with junk, and running up Lambda cost.

Required:
  - Validate lat/long are numeric, in range, and sanely bounded.
  - Reject coordinates outside AirNow's coverage area BEFORE any upstream call. A request for the middle of the Pacific should cost a 400, not an AirNow request.
  - Snap to a coarse grid so total cache key cardinality is finite and bounded.

title: Use GitHub Actions OIDC role assumption for AWS deploys
description: Assume an AWS role via OIDC rather than storing long-lived access keys in GitHub secrets -- no durable credential exists to leak, and access is scoped and auditable. Requires an IAM role with a trust policy for GitHub's OIDC provider, restricted to this repo.

title: Redact AirNow keys and raw coordinates before logging
description:
TWO separate leaks, same discipline.

1. CREDENTIAL. AirNow passes its API key as a URL query parameter (...&API_KEY=...), so logging the request URL writes the key straight into CloudWatch Logs, readable by anyone with log access for the whole retention period. This is the likeliest way this project leaks a key and it looks exactly like ordinary debug logging.

2. PRIVACY. Logging raw coordinates accumulates 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' for the retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database. Clients round coordinates before sending (see the client-side rounding task), but the service must not log even rounded values at full fidelity or tie them to source IPs.

Also ensure error responses and stack traces never echo the upstream URL or request headers back to clients. Needs a test asserting neither the key nor raw coordinates appear in log output.

title: Add gitleaks pre-commit hook and CI scan
description:
Two layers: a pre-commit hook catches a secret locally before a commit exists (cheapest possible point), and a CI job backstops commits made without the hook installed -- fresh clones, other machines, other agents.

CRITICAL -- must include a CUSTOM RULE for the AirNow key. GitHub's push protection and gitleaks' default rules both key on distinctive credential formats (AWS 'AKIA...', GitHub 'ghp_...', Stripe 'sk_live_...'). The AirNow key has no such distinctive prefix -- like most government API keys it is a generic token -- so NO pattern scanner will reliably catch a bare one. Default protection therefore covers the AWS and Apple credentials in our inventory but NOT the project's primary secret.

The custom rule must key on context rather than the token shape: assignments to AIRNOW_API_KEY / API_KEY, and any high-entropy token appearing near 'airnowapi.org'. Without this, the layered enforcement described in doc/DESIGN.md has a hole exactly where it matters most.

title: Enable GitHub push protection and secret scanning
description: Free on public repos. Blocks a push containing a recognized credential pattern before it reaches the remote -- the only layer that stops a leak from ever becoming public. Enable in repo settings for sbarber2/bluegull-aqi. Highest-value enforcement layer and takes about a minute.
close_reason: Verified enabled: secret_scanning=enabled, secret_scanning_push_protection=enabled on sbarber2/bluegull-aqi. GitHub enables both by default for public repos, so no change was needed -- confirmed via gh api rather than assumed. NOTE: secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns and secret_scanning_validity_checks remain disabled; a PATCH via gh api was accepted without error but did not apply them, so they need the web UI (Settings -> Code security) or may require GHAS. Tracked as a follow-up.

title: Implement perf baseline storage and regression gate
description:
Two independent checks per metric: an ABSOLUTE ceiling and a RELATIVE regression gate. They catch different failures -- the relative gate catches a sudden jump but is blind to the ratchet (drift 4% eleven times and you've doubled without ever failing a build); the absolute ceiling stops that.

Absolute ceilings (server-side latency, measured API Gateway receive -> response send):
  - Warm cached round-trip: p95 < 50ms, p50 < 25ms
  - Uncached round-trip, AirNow stubbed: p95 < 100ms
  - Cold start Init Duration: p50 < 600ms, investigate > 1s
  - p95 latency at 100 concurrent: within 2x the 10-concurrent p95
  - Error rate at 10 and 100 concurrent: < 0.1%
  - Cache hit ratio under steady-state load: > 95%

Relative gates: 5% on everything except cold start (~15%, variance is inherently larger). Compare percentiles over N>=100 samples, never single measurements.

Baseline lives in perf-baseline.json committed to the repo, so regressions appear as a reviewable diff and accepting an intentional regression is an explicit commit rather than a silent overwrite. Real end-to-end uncached latency (live AirNow) is recorded for observability but NOT gated -- it mostly measures AirNow, which we don't control. Client-observed latency likewise tracked but not gated (DNS/TLS/distance dominate; no code change fixes them).

title: Add AirNow stub/test mode for load testing
description: MANDATORY before any load test runs, not an optimization: driving 100 concurrent uncached requests at the live AirNow API would burn the project's quota and plausibly violate its terms. Env-gated test mode (or a reserved synthetic location) on the dev stage returns canned data in place of the upstream call, so load tests measure our overhead without touching AirNow.

title: Test concurrent cache-miss behavior against DynamoDB Local
description: Verify the stampede mitigation actually works: concurrent misses on the same key must produce exactly one upstream AirNow call, and an expired entry must be served immediately rather than blocking. Runs against DynamoDB Local -- no AWS needed.

title: Implement stale-while-revalidate + single-flight cache logic
description: The core horizontal-scaling mechanism. On a miss against an expired entry: serve the stale value immediately, and let exactly one request win a DynamoDB conditional-write lock to refresh it in the background. AirNow must see at most one call per location per TTL regardless of client concurrency. Cold-start-of-the-world (no entry at all) may block -- that's a once-per-location event. Cache TTL should align to AirNow's hourly publish schedule rather than being a rolling hour from first request.

title: Build native local runner for the proxy server
description: A thin script (Flask or plain http.server/wsgiref) serves the same core handler logic over HTTP on localhost -- e.g. 'make run-local' or 'python bin/run_local.py'. No Docker, no SAM CLI, no AWS deploy required to test manually. Reads the AirNow key from a local env var/.env file, not Secrets Manager/SSM, so nothing about local dev touches AWS.

title: Vendor DynamoDB Local and local start/stop script
description: Mirror Plant-Tracer's bin/local_services.py + vendored DynamoDBLocal.jar (see /Users/sbarber/git/Plant-Tracer/webapp/bin/) so the cache backend can be exercised locally and in CI without any AWS account. Same DynamoDB wire protocol as production, just pointed at a local endpoint via env var (endpoint_url).

title: Submit for App Review
description: Final App Store Connect submission and review pass.

title: Scaffold WidgetKit extension target
description: New extension target in the Xcode project, sharing the App Group and BluegullAQIKit with the container app.

title: Scaffold Xcode project with container app target
description: MenuBarExtra-based container app target, plus the BluegullAQIKit package dependency wired in.

title: Define shared models: AQIReading, PollutantReading, Location
description:
Common models both data-source clients decode into, so callers don't care which source answered.

MUST include the official EPA AQI category table as a single shared mapping -- not left for each UI target to define separately. Values below are verbatim from the AQI Technical Assistance Document (EPA 454/B-18-007, Sept 2018), Tables 1 and 2. These are binding by incorporation: the AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require values be 'disseminated in accordance with the AQI and corresponding RGB colors as directed in the Technical Assistance Document.'

  RANGE      DESCRIPTOR                      COLOR    RGB            HEX
  0-50       Good                            Green    0, 228, 0      #00E400
  51-100     Moderate                        Yellow   255, 255, 0    #FFFF00
  101-150    Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  Orange   255, 126, 0    #FF7E00
  151-200    Unhealthy                       Red      255, 0, 0      #FF0000
  201-300    Very Unhealthy                  Purple   143, 63, 151   #8F3F97
  301-500    Hazardous                       Maroon   126, 0, 35     #7E0023

GOTCHAS: Green is 0,228,0 -- NOT 0,255,0. Maroon is 126,0,35 -- not a generic dark red. Getting these subtly wrong is the most likely failure mode.

SPECIFY IN sRGB EXPLICITLY. On a wide-gamut Display P3 Mac, a color literal interpreted in the display's native color space renders visibly different values than EPA specified.

Full descriptor is 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups'; 'USG' is AirNow's own abbreviation for tight layouts (seen on airnow.gov's legend) and is acceptable where space genuinely requires it.

AQI values above 500 are 'Beyond the AQI' and need separate handling -- see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.
notes: AQI category scale is bounded at 500 per TAD Table 1 (301-500 Hazardous). Values above 500 are 'beyond the AQI scale' -- valid but off-scale data, not an error; see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. The model must represent that case rather than leaving it unmapped.

title: Scaffold BluegullAQIKit Swift package
description: Swift package shared by the container app and widget extension targets.

title: Deploy backend service to dev stage
description: First real deployment once handler, cache, secret storage, WAF, and CI are in place.

title: Add DynamoDB cache table with TTL to SAM template
description: Single table keyed by rounded lat/long (or zip), TTL attribute ~1hr, to collapse repeated client requests into one upstream AirNow call.

title: Store service AirNow key in SSM Parameter Store / Secrets Manager
description: Service's own AirNow API key in SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) or Secrets Manager, referenced by the Lambda execution role and resolved via SAM/CloudFormation dynamic reference at deploy time. Never in source, never in template.yaml, never as a CloudFormation parameter default, never in samconfig.toml parameter_overrides. See doc/DESIGN.md section 'Secrets & credentials' for the full policy and inventory.

title: Implement Lambda handler for AQI lookup
description: lat/long -> AirNow currentobservation/latLong proxy. Plain Lambda + API Gateway HTTP API (no Flask/Lambda Web Adapter -- this is a thin JSON proxy, not a multi-route app). Core lookup/cache logic must live in a plain Python function/module separate from the Lambda entry point, and the DynamoDB client's endpoint_url/region must come from env vars, so the exact same code path runs against production DynamoDB and against DynamoDB Local for local dev and tests.

title: Scaffold SAM project structure
description: service/template.yaml, samconfig.toml, src/, tests/ following Plant-Tracer's layout conventions (see /Users/sbarber/git/Plant-Tracer/webapp/template.yaml).

title: Create Apple Developer bundle IDs and App Group
description: Register bundle IDs for the container app and widget extension, and create the App Group used for shared cache storage between them.

title: Decide domain name for backend custom domain
description: DECIDED 2026-07-28: aqi.bluegull.org. Route53 hosted zone + ACM cert to be configured for it in service/template.yaml, same pattern as planttracer.com in Plant-Tracer's template.yaml. Unverified: whether bluegull.org already has a Route53 hosted zone in the target AWS account (see bluegull-aqi-8ef.4, still open) -- bluegull-aqi-q9r.6 should confirm this rather than assume it exists before wiring the SAM template.

title: Decide default data-source mode for fresh installs
description: Service mode (works immediately, no key needed) vs Direct mode (requires AirNow key up front, no dependency on BlueGull backend). doc/DESIGN.md currently leans Service but this is unconfirmed.

title: Register AirNow API key for backend service
description: Sign up at airnowapi.org for the key the Lambda service will use server-side. While there, confirm AirNow's published rate limits/ToS so the DynamoDB cache TTL can be sized correctly. Do NOT paste the key into a bd issue, commit message, or any repo file -- it goes straight into SSM Parameter Store / Secrets Manager, and into a gitignored .env for local dev.

title: Label displayed values as NowCast, not a spot reading
description:
AirNow's real-time observations are NowCast AQI -- EPA's endorsed method for relating short-term data to the AQI. It uses a VARIABLE averaging window: longer when air quality is stable, shorter when changing fast (PM2.5 ~12h stable / ~3h variable; ozone ~8h stable / ~1h variable).

So the number is a weighted average designed to track lived experience -- NOT an instantaneous sensor reading, and NOT the daily AQI (which requires a full 24 hours and is what agencies report for 'yesterday'). UI copy must not imply otherwise: avoid phrasing like 'right now' or 'current reading' that suggests a spot measurement.

'Current Air Quality' is the phrasing airnow.gov itself uses and is safe. This is a copy/labeling task, plus deciding whether to surface a brief explanation of NowCast somewhere reachable (natural fit alongside the preliminary-data disclaimer in the popover/expand view). See doc/DESIGN.md 'What the number is: NowCast, not a spot reading'.

title: Handle AQI > 500 (beyond the AQI scale) as valid data
description:
The category model currently has no representation for AQI above 500, so the default behavior is a blank/unknown category -- which would black out the app during exactly the conditions that produce such readings. That is the failure mode to design against.

RESOLVED: >500 is rare but REAL DATA, not an error.
  - TAD Table 1 bounds Hazardous at 301-500; above that is 'Beyond the AQI', where a value 'can still be computed to indicate relative magnitude' using the Hazardous breakpoints, and users should 'follow the recommendations for the Hazardous category'. NowCast handles it no differently. EPA would not document a computation for something that could only be a fault.
  - It has actually occurred in official reporting: Oregon DEQ recorded Bend above 500 on 2020-09-12 ('beyond the AQI scale' in their words), Newport 'well over 500', during that September's wildfires.
  - We never compute AQI (bluegull-aqi-10h.17), so anything received has already passed AirNow's own QA. Data trustworthiness is upstream of us; our obligation is to disseminate as received.

EARLIER ERROR CORRECTED: a previous version of this issue claimed airnow.gov diverged from the TAD by showing '301 +'. Wrong -- that came from a collapsed text extraction. The expanded AQI Legend panel shows '301 - 500  Hazardous' plus 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale'. Both sources agree; there is no conflict to resolve.

IMPLEMENT: display the actual value; keep maroon (#7E0023) and the Hazardous health guidance per the TAD's explicit direction; indicate it is beyond the scale, using AirNow's own phrasing ('Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale') rather than inventing wording. Do NOT clamp to 500 -- that would misrepresent the reading and conflicts with 'disseminated as received'.

SEPARATE CONCERN, handle distinctly: genuinely malformed values -- negative AQI, non-numeric, absurd magnitudes -- indicate a parse or transport fault rather than extreme air, and belong in an error state, not the beyond-the-scale path. Don't conflate the two.

Test with a fixture at e.g. AQI 650 to confirm it renders correctly rather than blanking.

title: Implement widget tap-to-expand detail view (attribution + disclaimer)
description:
Like Apple's own Weather widget: the whole widget is a tap target via WidgetKit's widgetURL, deep-linking into the container app, which shows a detail view in response. v1 scope is narrow and compliance-driven: attribution ('Data courtesy of {agency}') and the preliminary-data disclaimer, reusing content/view code from the menu bar popover (bluegull-aqi-e70.11) rather than building a third separate compliance surface.

This resolves the earlier open question of whether the widget needs attribution/disclaimer given the popover exists -- yes, it does, because a user may have the widget on their desktop without ever having opened the popover from the menu bar, so the widget needs its own reachable path to the same information. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' findings 1 and 2.

title: Implement menu bar popover (.window style)
description:
Clicking the menu bar status item opens a real SwiftUI view via MenuBarExtra's .window style (NOT the plain .menu dropdown-list style) -- a proper popover with layout space, similar in content to the widget: current AQI, full pollutant breakdown, and both compliance elements (attribution footer, preliminary-data disclaimer -- see bluegull-aqi-e70.10 and dc2.4, both retargeted to live here).

This is the guaranteed access point for those two compliance elements regardless of whether the user has ever placed the desktop widget on their screen -- the status item alone is too small for either, and the widget can't be relied on as the sole channel since many users may never add it. Likely also the natural home for reaching settings (mode toggle, key entry, pinned locations) via something like a gear icon, rather than those living in a separate always-open window.

title: Notify AirNow of this product (Data Exchange Guidelines form)
description:
AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines: 'publications, analyses, products... that rely on these data must be made known to the relevant... agencies and the EPA AirNow program.' The Guidelines PDF (docs.airnowapi.org/docs/DataUseGuidelines.pdf) is literally structured as a form for this -- Name/Title/Email/Phone/Organization/Date -- to be emailed to dmc@airnowtech.org. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' finding 4.

Administrative, not code: fill out and send the form once the project is far enough along to describe (app name, what it does, that it's a free Mac App Store app). Depends on the terms review sign-off since it doesn't make sense to notify AirNow of a product/architecture that review might still change.

title: Add in-product preliminary-data disclaimer
description:
AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines: 'the analysis results, displays, or products must indicate that these data are preliminary.' This has to be IN the product, not just documentation. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' finding 2.

CONCRETE HOMES, both required: the menu bar popover (bluegull-aqi-e70.11) and the widget's tap-to-expand detail view (bluegull-aqi-mtm.13) -- covers a user who only ever sees the menu bar, and a user who only ever sees the desktop widget. The iOS app precedent (About page via dropdown menu) is evidence of one acceptable placement, not proof it's required or sufficient -- see doc/DESIGN.md 'On using EPA's own apps as evidence'. Given both surfaces already carry attribution, showing the disclaimer alongside it (inline, or one tap deeper via an info affordance) is more conservative than the iOS app's buried-in-a-menu approach and costs little extra, but the final placement/wording call is Steve's.

title: Add 'Data courtesy of [agency]' attribution to menu bar popover
description:
Menu bar popover home for attribution -- see bluegull-aqi-e70.11. A persistent small footer, styled after the airnow.gov precedent ('Data courtesy of {agency}' + EPA/AirNow branding) -- see doc/DESIGN.md 'On using EPA's own apps as evidence' for why that precedent is suggestive, not dispositive, of what's actually required.

Surface the attribution text from bluegull-aqi-10h.15 in the popover. RESOLVED 2026-07-28: the widget also needs this, via its own tap-to-expand detail view (bluegull-aqi-mtm.13) rather than relying on the popover alone -- a user may never open the popover even with the widget on their desktop.

title: Derive two-tier attribution text from AirNow response data
description:
AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require credit to go FIRST to the specific state/local/tribal agency, THEN to AirNow/EPA. App precedent is evidence, not the standard itself (see doc/DESIGN.md 'On using EPA's own apps as evidence'): checked live against airnow.gov (2026-07-28, San Francisco), which shows a persistent small footer reading 'Data courtesy of / Bay Area Air District' -- the actual local agency name -- alongside a separate 'EPA and PARTNERS' logo lockup. That's useful evidence the specific agency-name field exists and is populated per location in AirNow's own data, not proof this particular wording/placement is what the guidelines require -- Steve's read of the actual text governs the final call.

Implementation: find the field in currentobservation/latLong (or a companion lookup, e.g. ReportingArea -> agency name) that supplies the agency name shown in this pattern. Produce a 'Data courtesy of {agency}' string per reading in BluegullAQIKit, paired with static EPA/AirNow branding as the second tier. If a location genuinely has no agency name in the response, that's the fallback case -- a generic class credit -- not the default design.

title: Enable Dependabot security updates
description: Currently DISABLED on sbarber2/bluegull-aqi -- confirmed via 'gh api /repos/sbarber2/bluegull-aqi --jq .security_and_analysis' on 2026-07-27. Covers both the Lambda Python dependencies and the Swift package dependencies once those exist. Independent of the AirNow terms question, so this can proceed any time.

title: Review Keychain item accessibility and access group
description: Confirm the AirNow key is stored with an appropriate accessibility class (e.g. AfterFirstUnlock rather than Always), is marked synchronizable for iCloud Keychain as intended, and that the access group scopes it to our app rather than leaving it broadly readable.

title: Bound App Group cache retention and review file protection
description: The App Group container holds the user's location history on disk -- the locations matter considerably more than the AQI values do. Bound retention rather than accumulating indefinitely, and review the file protection class on the container.

title: Rate-limit cache misses separately from overall requests
description: Stronger version of the cache-cardinality defense. Misses are what actually cost money and AirNow quota, so limiting them specifically is more targeted than an overall request cap. Build on top of the coordinate validation and grid-snapping, which are the cheaper first line.

title: Handle Apple signing secrets safely in CI
description: Signing certificate and App Store Connect API key stored as GitHub Actions encrypted secrets, imported into a temporary keychain at build time and torn down after -- never committed, never left in a persistent CI keychain.

title: Commit .env.example with placeholder values
description: Template documenting every env var the service needs (AirNow key, DynamoDB endpoint/region, log level) with obvious placeholder values -- never a real-looking key. Real .env is gitignored.

title: Re-tighten absolute perf ceilings against first real measurements
description: The absolute ceilings in doc/DESIGN.md are component-level estimates (~5-10ms API Gateway HTTP API overhead, ~1-3ms warm invoke, ~8-15ms DynamoDB GetItem with reused connection), not measurements -- nothing was deployed when they were written. Once the dev stage has real numbers, tighten the ceilings to match: a ceiling carrying 2.5x slack isn't doing much work. Expected healthy warm-cached p95 is ~20-30ms, so a 50ms ceiling likely wants to come down to ~35ms. Update both DESIGN.md and perf-baseline.json.

title: Add jittered refresh scheduling to client
description: Hourly refresh means every install would otherwise wake at the top of the hour and synchronize into a server-side spike. Each install derives a stable offset within the hour from a per-install value -- stable rather than re-randomized each refresh, so the interval stays consistent -- spreading load uniformly. Directly reduces peak load on the backend.

title: Gate module import time and package size locally (AWS-free cold-start proxy)
description: Import time and deployment package size are measurable with no deployment and correlate well with Init Duration. Gating them in the ordinary functional CI catches the most common cold-start regression -- someone adding a heavy dependency -- long before the nightly perf run does.

title: Add release-gated and nightly perf regression workflow
description: GitHub Actions: full perf/load suite against a deployed dev stage on release tags (the pass/fail gate) plus nightly for a drift trend line. Functional tests stay local and AWS-free on every push -- this tier is separate precisely because cold start requires real Lambda.

title: Build cold-start measurement harness
description: Read Init Duration from the CloudWatch Logs REPORT lines after forcing cold starts via fresh deploys. Collect a median over N samples -- single measurements are far too noisy to compare. Can only run against real Lambda; the native local runner has no Init phase.

title: Build k6 load test suite for 10 and 100 concurrent clients
description: k6 chosen for its native threshold support (http_req_duration: ['p(95)<...']), which expresses pass/fail gates directly with little custom scripting. Measures the horizontal-scaling response curve: warm cached round-trip, uncached round-trip with AirNow stubbed, throughput, error rate, and cache hit ratio at 10 and 100 concurrent.

title: Add CloudWatch metrics and alarms
description: p50/p95 latency, error rate, concurrent executions, throttles, and cache hit ratio. Cache hit ratio is the leading indicator for everything else -- if it drops, AirNow load and latency both rise.

title: Minimize Lambda cold start: package size and client init
description: Prefer the runtime-provided boto3 over vendoring a copy; keep dependencies light; create AWS clients at module scope so they're built once during Init and reused across warm invocations. Provisioned concurrency is the escape hatch if Init Duration becomes user-visible, not the default -- it bills continuously.

title: Configure Lambda/DynamoDB for horizontal scale in SAM template
description: DynamoDB on-demand billing mode (no capacity planning, autoscales). ARM64/Graviton Lambda architecture (cheaper, equal-or-better perf). Reserved concurrency -- see the cost circuit breaker task, which treats this as the PRIMARY defense against denial of wallet rather than merely a noisy-neighbor courtesy. Sharing an AWS account with Plant-Tracer also means a cost attack here can disrupt that project, a blast-radius argument bearing on the open AWS account decision.

title: Add XCUITest suite driving the menu bar app
description: xcodebuild test runs XCUITest, which launches the container app and drives it via the accessibility hierarchy; NSStatusItem menu bar extras are queryable. Cover settings flows, data-source mode toggling, and pinned-location management. Known cost: menu bar automation is finicky, and CI needs a logged-in GUI session plus TCC/accessibility permission for the test runner -- the classic 'passes locally, hangs in CI' trap. Budget time for CI permission wrangling.

title: Add widget snapshot regression tests with golden PNGs
description: Golden PNGs committed to the repo, compared per run. Use pointfreeco/swift-snapshot-testing (supports SwiftUI on macOS) or a small hand-rolled ImageRenderer + PNG-comparison helper; test-only dependency either way, does not ship in the App Store build. Cover the failure modes this widget is prone to: AQI 500 vs 5 changing layout, full pollutant breakdown overflowing the large widget, missing-data and stale-cache states, light/dark mode, Dynamic Type sizes.

title: Build ImageRenderer harness to render widget views to PNG
description: A WidgetKit widget view is just a SwiftUI view taking a timeline entry -- it renders headlessly via ImageRenderer (macOS 13+) with no widget host. Harness renders small/medium/large layouts from fixture entries to PNGs on demand, for both snapshot tests and direct visual inspection by a human or an image-capable agent. Runs from the command line, no GUI interaction.

title: Manual verification: real widget host and background refresh budget
description: Narrow residue that automation genuinely can't cover (snapshot tests cover all three layouts headlessly; see the ImageRenderer/snapshot tasks). Verify by hand: the widget installs and appears correctly in the real widget host on the desktop, and hourly background refresh actually fires under WidgetKit's system-managed budget -- which plays out over hours of real system scheduling, not in a test run.

title: Manual verification: permission prompts and cross-Mac Keychain sync
description: Narrow residue that automation genuinely can't cover (XCUITest covers the settings/mode/pinned-location flows; see the XCUITest task). Verify by hand on a real Mac: the CoreLocation permission (TCC) dialog appears and is handled correctly, and the AirNow key entered on one Mac shows up on a second Mac via iCloud Keychain sync. Requires two physical Macs for the sync half.

title: Add App Intents perform() unit tests
description: Unit test the WidgetConfigurationIntent's perform() logic directly (pinned-location selection).

title: Add TimelineProvider unit tests using fixture App Group cache state
description: Feed the TimelineProvider a fixture App Group cache state and assert on the produced timeline entries -- doesn't require the widget to actually render.

title: Set up GitHub Actions CI workflow for mac-app (xcodebuild test)
description: xcodebuild test on a macos-latest runner covering three suites: BluegullAQIKit unit tests, widget snapshot tests (headless ImageRenderer, no widget host needed), and the XCUITest suite driving the menu bar app. The XCUITest job needs a logged-in GUI session plus TCC/accessibility permission for the test runner -- expect CI permission wrangling. Does not cover TCC permission dialogs, cross-Mac iCloud Keychain sync, or real background-refresh scheduling; those stay manual.

title: Add Lambda handler contract tests using API Gateway event fixtures
description: Feed the Lambda entry point sample API Gateway HTTP API event fixtures (like Plant-Tracer's events/event.json) and assert on the wrapped JSON response, so the thin-handler-over-core-logic split is actually verified, not just structural.

title: Write privacy nutrition label content
description: App Store privacy label covering location data usage.

title: Configure App Sandbox entitlements
description: Location, network client, and App Group entitlements for both the container app and widget extension targets.

title: Design rate-limit-exceeded UX for service mode
description: What the user sees when the anonymous/IP-based WAF throttle kicks in on the backend, and how to nudge toward Direct mode.

title: Handle stale-cache/offline states in UI
description: Menu bar and widget both need a clear state for 'no network' / 'cache older than expected' rather than silently showing stale data.

title: Implement App Intents configuration for pinned location selection
description: WidgetConfigurationIntent letting each widget instance pick 'current location' or a specific pinned location.

title: Implement TimelineProvider reading App Group cache
description: Reads whatever the container app last wrote; does not fetch network or location itself.

title: Wire container app fetch results into App Group cache
description: Container app performs the actual network fetch (widget extensions have restricted background networking) and writes results the widget's TimelineProvider will read.

title: Build settings UI: pinned locations management
description: Add/remove/rename pinned zip codes or addresses, geocoded via LocationResolver.

title: Implement menu bar current AQI display
description: The menu bar extra (status item) itself -- the small always-visible sliver in the system menu bar. Shows current overall AQI as text/icon only; no room here for attribution or the disclaimer, see the popover task (bluegull-aqi-e70.11) for those.

title: Build settings UI: AirNow API key entry
description: Entry/edit/clear for the user's own AirNow API key, backed by the Keychain helper.

title: Implement location permission request flow
description: CoreLocation authorization request/handling for current-location mode.

title: Build settings UI: data-source mode toggle
description: Switch between Service mode and Direct mode. Default choice depends on the open decision in doc/DESIGN.md.

title: Write unit tests for BluegullAQIKit
description: Cover model decoding for both clients, cache TTL behavior (injected fake clock), and Keychain round-trip. Both clients' networking is stubbed via URLProtocol -- no live AirNow or backend calls in CI. Includes a contract test that feeds AirNowDirectClient and BluegullServiceClient structurally-equivalent fixture payloads and asserts they decode to identical model instances, proving the 'client code doesn't care which source answered' design claim.

title: Implement App Group shared cache
description: 1-hour TTL, keyed by location. Written by the container app after a successful fetch; read by the widget's TimelineProvider.

title: Implement Keychain helper for AirNow API key
description: Reads/writes the user's AirNow API key as an iCloud-synced Keychain item (syncs across the user's Macs under their Apple ID).

title: Implement LocationResolver
description: Wraps CoreLocation for current-location mode, and CLGeocoder/MapKit for resolving user-pinned zip/address locations (no backend geocoding endpoint needed). Exposed behind a protocol so tests can inject a fake location/geocoder -- CI can't exercise real GPS or live geocoding.

title: Implement AirNowDirectClient
description: Calls AirNow's currentobservation/latLong (and forecast/latLong later) directly using the Keychain-stored user key.

title: Implement BluegullServiceClient
description: Calls the BlueGull backend Lambda endpoint; must decode into the same models as AirNowDirectClient.

title: Write unit/integration tests for Lambda handler
description: Integration tests run against DynamoDB Local (not mocks/moto), matching Plant-Tracer's approach -- same DynamoDB wire protocol as production, just a local endpoint. No AWS account or deployment required to run the test suite.

title: Set up GitHub Actions deploy workflow
description: Manual trigger (workflow_dispatch) or tag-gated deploy to a dev stage -- not auto-deployed on merge, matching Plant-Tracer's currently-manual deploy-*.yml-OFF workflows until the service is proven out.

title: Configure Route53 + ACM custom domain in template.yaml
description: Domain: aqi.bluegull.org (decided bluegull-aqi-8ef.3). Route53 hosted zone + ACM cert, same pattern as planttracer.com in Plant-Tracer's template.yaml. First confirm whether bluegull.org already has a Route53 hosted zone in the target AWS account, or whether one needs to be created/delegated -- don't assume it exists.

title: Set up GitHub Actions CI workflow
description: Lint, pytest, sam validate/sam build on push, mirroring Plant-Tracer's ci-cd.yml. CI starts DynamoDB Local before running tests (like Plant-Tracer's 'start local DynamoDB endpoint' step) -- no AWS account or deployment needed for CI.

title: Add AWS WAFv2 rate-based rule for per-IP throttling
description: HTTP API (v2) doesn't support REST API v1 usage-plan/API-key throttling, so use a WAFv2 rate-based rule attached to the API Gateway instead. Known tradeoff: coarser than per-install keys (shared IPs behind CGNAT), chosen deliberately.

title: Decide AWS account target
description: Reuse the same AWS account as Plant-Tracer, or use a separate account for billing/IAM isolation.

title: Integration polish
description: Cross-cutting UX: stale/offline handling, rate-limit UX, refresh budget tuning.

title: App Store submission prep
description: Sandbox entitlements, privacy nutrition label, screenshots, and the App Review submission itself.

title: Menu bar app
description: Container app: MenuBarExtra showing current overall AQI, settings UI, location permission flow, and the actual network fetch (widget extension only reads cached results).

title: Widget extension
description: WidgetKit desktop widget (macOS 14+): current AQI + full pollutant breakdown, configurable per-instance for pinned locations.

title: BluegullAQIKit shared package
description: Swift package shared by the menu bar app and widget extension: models, both data-source clients, Keychain, location resolver, App Group cache.

title: Backend service MVP
description: AWS SAM Lambda + API Gateway caching proxy in front of AirNow, deployed similarly to Plant-Tracer's webapp. See doc/DESIGN.md Backend service design.

title: Prerequisites & open decisions
description: Accounts, keys, and decisions that need to be resolved before or alongside implementation. See doc/DESIGN.md Open Questions.

title: Use 'particle pollution' rather than 'particulate matter' in UI copy
description:
From the TAD FAQ: 'Based on focus group testing by EPA, people better understand and prefer the term particle pollution than particulate matter.'

A copy preference, not a requirement -- EPA's own research on what the public actually understands, which is worth following for an app whose purpose is public health communication. Applies to pollutant labels in the widget, popover, and expand view. 'PM2.5' / 'PM10' remain fine as compact labels where space is tight; this is about the spelled-out form.

title: Keep AirNow contact info current (ongoing obligation)
description:
AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines: 'Data users' contact information must be kept current for the purposes of informing users of these data about any program or product updates and/or problems.' See doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' finding 5.

This is a standing obligation, not a one-time task with a natural 'done' state -- there's nothing to build. Filed so it's not forgotten: revisit whenever the registered contact email/organization details change, and again as a checklist item during App Store submission prep when the project's public-facing contact info gets finalized.

title: Verify current WAF rate-based rule minimums
description: The design references per-IP rate limiting without pinning down the current minimum threshold and evaluation window AWS supports for rate-based rules; these have changed over time. Confirm the actual numbers before relying on them, since they determine how much protection the rule really provides.

title: Evaluate CloudFront in front of the API
description: Deliberately deferred, not rejected. The response is identical for everyone in a region and changes hourly -- close to an ideal CDN workload. CloudFront would absorb most traffic at the edge before it reaches Lambda, cutting cost and attack surface together, and offers better DDoS absorption than raw API Gateway. Not worth the complexity pre-launch; this is the natural first move if scale materializes. Revisit when sustained traffic justifies it or if cost-attack exposure becomes a live concern.

title: Enable secret scanning non-provider patterns and validity checks
description: Both remain disabled on sbarber2/bluegull-aqi. A PATCH to /repos/sbarber2/bluegull-aqi with security_and_analysis was accepted without error but did not change them, so they likely need the web UI (Settings -> Code security) or require GitHub Advanced Security. Non-provider patterns broadens detection beyond known-provider formats; validity checks flag whether a detected secret is still live. Lower priority than the gitleaks custom rule, which is what actually covers the AirNow key -- see the gitleaks task. Expect more false positives with non-provider patterns on, which is cheap for a repo this size.

title: Add Makefile targets wrapping the test suites
description: Follow Plant-Tracer's Makefile idiom: make test-swift (xcodebuild test), make snapshots (regenerate/inspect widget PNGs), make test (everything including the service-side pytest suite). Everything runnable from a bash command line.

title: Document local run instructions in service/README.md
description: How to start DynamoDB Local and the native runner, and hit it with curl -- no AWS account or deploy needed.

title: Prepare App Store screenshots
description: Menu bar and widget (all three sizes) screenshots for the App Store listing.

title: Tune background-refresh budget for WidgetKit timeline
description: Fit the hourly refresh target within WidgetKit's system-managed background refresh budget.

title: Build widget UI: large family layout
description: Current AQI plus full pollutant breakdown, per doc/DESIGN.md widget scope. Must use the official EPA AQI category colors from BluegullAQIKit's shared mapping, not a custom palette -- see doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' item 3.

title: Build widget UI: small family layout
description: Compact current-AQI view. Must use the official EPA AQI category colors from BluegullAQIKit's shared mapping, not a custom palette -- see doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' item 3.

title: Build widget UI: medium family layout
description: Current AQI plus a few headline pollutants. Must use the official EPA AQI category colors from BluegullAQIKit's shared mapping, not a custom palette -- see doc/DESIGN.md 'AirNow terms review' item 3.

title: Display sensitive groups and cautionary statements (POST-v1)
description:
DEFERRED past v1 -- decided 2026-07-28. Not a rejection: the content is valuable and the task stays open, just not in the first release.

TAD Table 3 (pollutant-specific sensitive groups) and Table 4 (cautionary statements per pollutant per AQI category) supply authoritative health-guidance text -- e.g. for PM2.5 at Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups: 'People with heart or lung disease, older adults, children, and people of lower socioeconomic status should reduce prolonged or heavy exertion.'

NOT REQUIRED OF US: those are reporting obligations on agencies when AQI > 100, and we are a downstream redistributor, not a reporting agency. That is what makes deferring it defensible -- v1 ships compliant without it. (Compare the attribution and preliminary-data disclaimer tasks, which ARE obligations and gate App Store submission.)

WHEN PICKED UP -- first check whether the AirNow API already returns this text (it may, via health-message or action-day fields). Displaying what the API returns is strongly preferable to embedding TAD table text: it stays current if EPA revises the language, and it honors 'disseminated as received'. If we do embed TAD text, it must be verbatim and unaltered.

Natural home is the post-v1 richer detail view (bluegull-aqi-mtm.15) rather than the v1 expand view, which is deliberately scoped to compliance content only. Note the app's health-protective purpose argues for this eventually -- the TAD states the AQI exists 'to inform people about their air quality so they can take steps to protect their health', especially above AQI 100.

title: Expand widget detail view with richer API data (POST-v1)
description:
DEFERRED -- explicitly not for the first release. Steve's framing: 'good scope creep... defer it.'

Once bluegull-aqi-mtm.14 exists (tap-to-expand -> detail view, v1 scope: attribution + disclaimer only), that same view is a natural place to show meaningfully more than the widget face does -- more like Apple Weather's expanded view (trends, forecast, additional pollutant detail, historical data) than a compliance-only screen. Deliberately unspecced beyond that for now; flesh out scope when it's actually picked up post-v1, informed by whatever AirNow endpoints (e.g. forecast, which the v1 data-scope decision chose not to fetch) seem worth adding at that point.

title: Investigate App Attest support on native macOS
description: UNVERIFIED: App Attest / DeviceCheck is well-established on iOS, but native macOS support is unconfirmed. If supported, it is the real answer to 'only our app may call this API' and would meaningfully change the abuse picture for an otherwise unauthenticated public endpoint. Do NOT design around it until confirmed. Research task only -- outcome is a yes/no plus a sketch of what adopting it would require.

title: Consider branch protection on main (PR-only merges)
description:
DEFERRED 2026-07-27 as premature -- with no code and no CI yet, branch protection is friction without benefit. Revisit when there is a real branch workflow or something worth gating review on, which naturally coincides with CI existing and producing status checks to require.

Decisions still open when this is picked up:
  - enforce_admins: should the rule bind the repo owner too (strong guarantee, deliberate friction for emergency pushes) or allow admin bypass (advisory only, since the owner is currently the sole committer)?

Already settled:
  - Required approving reviews must be 0. GitHub does not permit approving your own PR, so requiring 1 on a solo repo makes every merge impossible without a second account or an admin bypass.
  - Also block force-push and deletion on main.
  - Required status checks are the main source of value here; add them once CI workflows exist.

Verify afterward that 'bd dolt push' still works. Beads syncs to refs/dolt/data, which is outside refs/heads/ and should be unaffected by a main branch rule -- but confirm rather than assume.

title: Investigate whether a CLI exists to force an installed widget timeline reload
description: Unverified assumption flagged in doc/DESIGN.md: it is not known whether a supported command-line tool can force an installed widget to reload its timeline (as opposed to WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines() called from app code). Nothing in the plan depends on it -- this is a nice-to-have that would tighten the manual background-refresh verification loop. Confirm before relying on it; do not assume it exists.
